heading: Kyiv visit and 100-year treaty (January 2025)
body: On January 16, 2025, Starmer made an unannounced visit to Kyiv — his first trip to Ukraine since becoming Prime Minister some six months earlier — to sign a surprise 100-year military and economic treaty, announcing his travel with train journey photographs made necessary by the war-imposed no-fly zone.[n] Ahead of meetings with President [[volodymyr-zelensky|Volodymyr Zelensky]], he said he would sign the [[uk-ukraine-100-year-partnership|100 Year Partnership]], hailed as a historic arrangement to continue supporting Ukraine and invest in both countries' futures, formalising an "unbreakable bond" between the two nations.[n] Badlands commentary attributed the timing to fear that Donald Trump would pull all Americans out of Ukraine and leave the coalition without men or resources, with the treaty serving to prop up morale.[n]

heading: January 2025: UK treaty and Polish election row
body: Zelensky hosted British Prime Minister [[keir-starmer|Sir Keir Starmer]] in Kyiv on January 16, 2025 for the signing of the [[uk-ukraine-100-year-partnership|UK–Ukraine 100 Year Partnership]], a military and economic treaty formalising an "unbreakable bond" between the two countries.[n] The same week, politicians from Poland's [[law-and-justice|Law and Justice]] party accused him of interfering in their country's presidential election.[n] The accusation followed Zelensky's response to PiS candidate [[karol-nawrocki|Karol Nawrocki]], who had said Kyiv could have no future in the EU or NATO until Ukraine took responsibility for the WWII [[volhynia-massacres|Volhynia massacres]]: "If Ukraine is not in the EU and not in NATO, if there are no security guarantees for Ukraine, then Pan Nawrocki should start training, because it may turn out that he will have to take up arms."[n] The remarks, made in an interview with local media during a visit to Poland, sparked outrage there.[n]

heading: Invoked in UK–Ukraine treaty commentary (2025)
body: Badlands commentary on the January 2025 [[uk-ukraine-100-year-partnership|UK–Ukraine 100 Year Partnership]] invoked the former Pale of Settlement — corresponding to modern-day Ukraine — as a locus of the rivalry between the Prussian elite and Russia.[n] The argument held that most Prussian oligarchs eventually left the continent for London and joined the British aristocracy, some German and some Russian Jews from the Pale region, alongside Austrian Jews such as the Rothschilds, all merging into a banking cabal the author traced back to Venice.[n]

heading: Border penalties decree (January 2025)
body: In January 2025 the Vatican City State enacted stiffer penalties on anyone entering its territory or violating its airspace without permission, through a [[vatican-border-penalties-decree|decree]] signed by Cardinal Fernando Vérgez Alzaga, president of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State.[n] Violators face fines of 10,000 to 25,000 euros and prison sentences of one to four years.[n] The Vatican is the world's only completely walled-in sovereign territory; all of its entry points except the Saint Anna gate are locked from dusk until dawn, and the gates are manned by the Swiss Guard with armed gendarmes nearby.[n]

heading: 2020 election questioning commentary (January 2025)
body: In a January 16, 2025 piece, The Federalist argued that Republicans need a forceful answer to Democrats' questions at Senate confirmation hearings about whether Donald Trump "lost" the 2020 election.[n] The publication contended the query contains an undefined term — "lost" — that means different things to Trump supporters and to anti-Trump inquisitors: if it merely means Joe Biden became president, the answer is obviously yes, as nominee Pam Bondi repeatedly and expressly attested.[n] What Dick Durbin, Richard Blumenthal and others demanding a yes-or-no answer actually sought, the argument ran, was a concession that Trump's election challenges were frivolous, unfounded or wrong — the same trap earlier set for then-Senator [[jd-vance|J.D. Vance]] by the legacy media.[n]

heading: Kobayashi Maru framing (January 2025)
body: Badlands contributor Burning Bright noted in January 2025 that Musk had begun routinely using the [[kobayashi-maru|Kobayashi Maru]] refrain in reference to the position the sociopolitical establishment had been placed in on a mass psychological level as the Trump era rose to new heights.[n] Separately, Musk was co-leader with [[vivek-ramaswamy|Vivek Ramaswamy]] of the Department of Government Efficiency panel, the assignment that had prompted Ramaswamy to withdraw from consideration for Ohio's Senate seat in November 2024.[n]

heading: Trump interview on the Gaza deal (January 2025)
body: In a podcast interview with Bongino shortly before his second inauguration, President-elect Donald Trump discussed the Gaza ceasefire, saying: "We changed the course of it, and we changed it fast, and frankly, it better be done before I take the oath of office."[n] Trump added, "We shook hands, and we signed certain documents, but it better be done."[n]

heading: Discipline in the second Trump operation (January 2025)
body: Reporting ahead of Donald Trump's second inauguration described Trump as equipped with "a highly capable chief of staff in Susie Wiles, who has infused more discipline into his operation," a key reason "Trump 2.0" was assessed as better set up to succeed than the 2017 administration.[n] Former press secretary [[sean-spicer|Sean Spicer]] framed the contrast in terms of "the people, the process and the priorities," saying the incoming team was "in a totally different league than we were in 2016."[n]

heading: Threat to quit over the ceasefire deal (January 2025)
body: Ben Gvir's party threatened to quit the Israeli government if the cabinet approved the hostage-ceasefire deal in January 2025.[n] Analysis at the time held that Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition would maintain a Knesset majority even without Ben Gvir's party, though it would fall to a minority if [[bezalel-smotrich|Bezalel Smotrich]]'s [[religious-zionism-party|Religious Zionism]] also followed through on its own threats to depart; opposition parties pledged to support the coalition so long as it advanced the deal.[n]

heading: Coalition leverage over the ceasefire deal (January 2025)
body: During the January 2025 Gaza ceasefire finalization, Smotrich's [[religious-zionism-party|Religious Zionism]] party was reported to be weighing departure from Benjamin Netanyahu's government over the hostage deal.[n] While the coalition would retain a Knesset majority without [[itamar-ben-gvir|Itamar Ben Gvir]]'s party alone, the additional loss of Religious Zionism would reduce it to a minority — a configuration that left Netanyahu dependent on opposition parties, which promised support so long as the government advanced the deal.[n]
